operations.name: Ben Fletcher

expected.charges: Conspiracy under the Espionage Act — opposing World War I (1918 Chicago IWW mass trial)
expected.sentence:
Ten years at Leavenworth; sentence commuted in 1922 and pardoned by President Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1933

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted August 1918

ADMITTED TO BAIL, APRIL 2, 1919. The Federal Circuit Court of Appeals ordered thirty-eight of the men convicted in the Chicago mass trial released on bail pending its review of the case; the bonds ran from $5,000 to $10,000, with Haywood alone required to provide $15,000. Fifty-five others convicted in the same case did not seek bail. The order is not the release: each man left Leavenworth when his bond was actually furnished, which for those whose dates are recorded here fell between April 28 and September 28, 1919. Reported in the New York Times and across the wire services, April 3, 1919.

operations.source: Primary Senate Document159, Government Prosecutions Under the Espionage Act (1922): https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/SERIALSET-07987_00_00-063-0159-0000/pdf/SERIALSET-07987_00_00-063-0159-0000.pdf . Printedpage8 individually gives BenFletcher ten-year Leavenworth term and fine. Bail order not actual departure, and documented intervening bond release prevents assuming one continuous interval. No custody endpoints invented.
